topic: Why Chile is so long and thin, and why landlocked Bolivia still has a navy

sources.title: Boundary treaty of 1881 between Chile and Argentina

claims.text: Chile extends 4,270 km north to south but averages only 177 km wide.
claims.quote: from north to south, the country extends 4,270 km (2,653 mi) , and yet it only averages 177 km (110 mi) in width; Chile measures 2,653 miles (4,270 km) from north to south; the country is only 110 miles (177 km) across, on average

claims.text: The 1881 treaty with Argentina put the border on the highest summits of the Andes that divide the waters.
claims.quote: The boundary-line shall run in that extent over the highest summits of the said Cordilleras which divide the waters; Chile is as narrow as it is because of the Andes Mountains, which separate it from Argentina

claims.text: The War of the Pacific began over a nitrate taxation dispute between Bolivia and Chile; Peru was drawn in by a secret alliance with Bolivia.
claims.quote: The direct cause of the war was a nitrate taxation dispute between Bolivia and Chile, with Peru being drawn in due to its secret alliance with Bolivia; The War of the Pacific grew out of a dispute between Chile and Bolivia over control of a part of the Atacama desert

claims.text: Nitrate and guano were valued as fertilizer (and saltpeter for explosives).
claims.quote: the value of guano and nitrate as fertilizer and the role of saltpeter in explosives; their use as fertilizer and as a key ingredient in explosives made the area strategically valuable

claims.text: On 14 February 1879 Chile's forces occupied the Bolivian port of Antofagasta.
claims.quote: 14 February 1879, Chile's armed forces occupied without resistance the Bolivian port city of Antofagasta; claimed the port city of Antofagasta without a fight

claims.text: Chile acquired Peru's Tarapacá and Bolivia's Litoral, turning Bolivia into a landlocked country.
claims.quote: Chile acquired the Peruvian territory of Tarapacá , the disputed Bolivian department of Litoral (turning Bolivia into a landlocked country ); Bolivia lost its nitrate-rich coastal region and became a land-locked state

claims.text: Landlocked since the war, Bolivia keeps a navy with a presence on Lake Titicaca, and it also patrols rivers; about 5,000 personnel as of 2018.
claims.quote: Bolivia also maintains a naval presence on Lake Titicaca; As of 2018, the Bolivian Navy had approximately 5,000 personnel; the Bolivian Navy extensively patrols Lake Titicaca and 5,000 miles of navigable rivers; keeping watch over Lake Titicaca, 3,800 metres above sea level

claims.text: Every 23 March Bolivia marks the Day of the Sea for the coast lost to Chile.
claims.quote: an annual celebration in Bolivia that observes the loss of Litoral Department during the 1879–1883 War of the Pacific with Chile; The day is celebrated on 23 March; particularly acute in Bolivia on March 23rd, the ‘Day of the Sea’, which marks the annexation of its shoreline

myths.myth: Bolivia's navy has nothing to do and only sails a lake.
myths.truth: It also patrols about 5,000 miles of rivers against smugglers and floods; the script says the lake is where it keeps a presence, not its only water.
